bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 5251 (curl): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer_ftp [asan].
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `gt_results/arvo_5251/_work/src/curl` / static parse of the staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 817-byte `poc` with SHA-256 `a5f78852ee518f32703762620d5f59c5894f35986dc062d05394f7d5328c07fe`. A static TLV parse shows type `1` URL bytes `ftp:/%f26.0X0.1:8991/[-list/*[!*-]*-]`, type `31` (`SECOND_RESPONSE0`) length 570 carrying the FTP `LIST` payload, and type `33` (`WILDCARDMATCH`) raw value `0x00c40003`, which `lib/url.c:2965` treats as true because any non-zero `long` enables wildcard mode. `init_wc_data()` duplicates the trailing wildcard component `*[!*-]*-]` into `wildcard->pattern` and installs `Curl_ftp_parselist()` as the LIST-body callback. The saved LIST payload begins with `total 20`, so `Curl_ftp_parselist()` selects the UNIX parser, allocates `finfo->b_data` for one listing record, and in `PL_UNIX_FILENAME` records `parser->item_offset`, overwrites the terminating newline with `0`, and stores `parser->offsets.filename` before `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` aliases `finfo->filename`. While filtering that parsed entry, `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` calls `Curl_fnmatch(wc->pattern, finfo->filename)`. The pattern's leading `*` retries the subpattern on progressively shorter filename suffixes until a recursive call evaluates `[!*-]*-]` with `s` at the filename terminator. `setcharset()` makes that bracket expression a negated class, so the `found` computation flips false to true on `*s == '\0'`. The vulnerable `if(found)` branch then executes `p = pp + 1; s++;`, moving `s` one byte past the heap buffer allocated for the current LIST item in `Curl_ftp_parselist()`. On the next iteration the remaining `*` arm rereads `*s` at `lib/curl_fnmatch.c:326`, and AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read with stack `loop -> loop -> ftp_pl_insert_finfo` and allocation context `Curl_ftp_parselist:358`.

source.description: Source. `init_wc_data()` splits the attacker-controlled FTP URL at the last slash and duplicates the trailing wildcard component into `wildcard->pattern`, the exact pattern later parsed by `Curl_fnmatch()`.
source.value_from: A static parse of the staged `gt_results/arvo_5251/poc` shows type-1 URL bytes `ftp:/%f26.0X0.1:8991/[-list/*[!*-]*-]`. The final path component after the last slash is `*[!*-]*-]`, so `last_slash` at this statement points to exactly that wildcard string.
source.note: This is the first project statement that materializes the vulnerability-relevant pattern buffer. The libFuzzer entry and the TLV parser are the unscored harness boundary; the non-zero `WILDCARDMATCH` option that makes this path reachable is recorded in `reachability_checkpoints.parser_admitted`.

root_cause.description: Missing guard. After a negated bracket class has turned `found` true on `*s == '\0'`, `loop()` still executes `s++` as though a real string byte had been consumed. That moves `s` one byte past the heap-backed filename buffer.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this path to advance only when `*s` is non-zero: `if(*s) s++;` with the comment `don't advance if we're matching on an empty string`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. On the next `*` iteration after step 11, `loop()` rereads `*s`; because `s` already points one byte past the filename buffer, this check dereferences heap memory out of bounds.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `lib/curl_fnmatch.c:326` on address `0x60f0000001e0`, 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x60f000000130, 0x60f0000001e0)` allocated at `Curl_ftp_parselist:358`.

parser_admitted.description: Parser admission. After wildcard mode is enabled and the URL has been split into path and pattern, `init_wc_data()` replaces the normal body callback with `Curl_ftp_parselist()`, so subsequent attacker-controlled data-connection bytes are fed into the FTP LIST parser that reaches `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()`.
parser_admitted.note: The PoC's type-33 raw value `0x00c40003` is non-zero, so `Curl_setopt()` sets `data->set.wildcard_enabled = TRUE` at `lib/url.c:2965`, `Curl_pretransfer()` copies that into `data->state.wildcardmatch` at `lib/transfer.c:1350`, and wildcard handling is initialized before this callback replacement occurs.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement makes `finfo->filename` alias the current parsed LIST item's NUL-terminated name inside `finfo->b_data`, the heap buffer later overread through `s`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The PoC's type-31 second-socket TLV is a 570-byte FTP LIST payload. In the saved UNIX parser path, `Curl_ftp_parselist()` allocates `finfo->b_data` at line 358, copies the record bytes into it, then records `parser->item_offset`, writes `0` over the terminating newline, and stores `parser->offsets.filename` at line 723 before `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` exposes the filename through this pointer.
tainted_value_origin.note: The exact visible basename at the crashing call is not needed to close the chain: the leading `*` retry logic in `loop()` eventually tests the terminating NUL of whichever `finfo->filename` is under comparison.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is closed from the staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, reproduction report, and static TLV parsing only.

Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds the exact missing `if(*s)` guard before advancing `s` after a successful bracket-class match.

The type-31 LIST payload is malformed and noisy, and Stage 02 does not rerun curl with probes to recover the exact directory-entry spelling at the crashing call. The causal chain does not require that spelling because the leading `*` retry logic inevitably reaches the terminating NUL of the compared filename.

coarse_trace.summary: `init_wc_data()` duplicates the attacker-controlled wildcard suffix `*[!*-]*-]` into `wildcard->pattern` and routes FTP LIST bodies into `Curl_ftp_parselist()`.

`Curl_ftp_parselist()` selects the UNIX LIST parser for the saved payload, allocates a heap buffer for one directory entry, copies the attacker-controlled bytes into it, and finalizes the filename by NUL-terminating it and storing `parser->offsets.filename`.
`ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` uses that stored offset to alias `finfo->filename`, defaults the callback to `Curl_fnmatch()`, and matches the parsed filename against `wc->pattern`.

The leading `*` eventually retries the tail `[!*-]*-]` on the filename's terminating NUL; the negated bracket class incorrectly turns that NUL into a match, `s++` steps one byte past the heap buffer, and the next `*s` check overreads at line 326.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The final URL path component is duplicated into `wildcard->pattern`. For the exact witness, the type-1 URL TLV ends with `/[-list/*[!*-]*-]`, so `last_slash` points to `*[!*-]*-]`, the wildcard pattern later parsed by `loop()`.

Wildcard transfers do not stream LIST bodies directly to the user callback. This step installs `Curl_ftp_parselist()` and passes `conn` as callback data, so the attacker-controlled data-connection payload from the type-31 TLV is parsed as a directory listing.

The saved type-31 LIST payload starts with `t` from `total 20`, not a digit, so the parser sets `parser->os_type = OS_TYPE_UNIX`. That control choice routes the record through the UNIX filename state machine rather than the WinNT parser.

For the current LIST item, the parser allocates `finfo->b_data` and appends each incoming byte `c` from the attacker-controlled LIST payload into that heap buffer. AddressSanitizer later identifies the allocation at line 358 as the 176-byte region that is overread.

In the UNIX filename arm selected at step 3, the first non-space filename byte records `parser->item_offset`, and when the record ends the parser overwrites the terminating newline with `0` and stores that saved start offset in `parser->offsets.filename`. This is the source-level transition that turns raw LIST bytes in `finfo->b_data` into a NUL-terminated filename slice immediately before `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` runs.

Using the offset and NUL-termination state from step 5, `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` makes `finfo->filename` alias the filename slice inside the same heap buffer. This pointer becomes the `string` argument later bound to `s` in `Curl_fnmatch()`.

The parser resolves the default callback to `Curl_fnmatch()` and calls it with the heap pattern from step 1 and the parsed filename alias from step 6. The saved ASan stack places this call site immediately below the two `loop()` frames.

The pattern starts with `*`, so the caller frame keeps retrying this recursive call while advancing `s` through progressively shorter filename suffixes. On the crashing retry, `p + 1` points to `[!*-]*-]` and `s` already points to the terminator of the filename slice from steps 5-6.

For the subpattern `[!*-]*-]`, `setcharset()` consumes the bracket expression `[!*-]`, returns success with `pp` on the closing `]`, sets the negate flag `charset[CURLFNM_NEGATE]`, and records literal members for `*` and `-`.

Because step 8 has moved the recursive call onto the empty suffix of the filename, `*s == '\0'`. No direct charset or character-class test matches `\0` for `[!*-]`, so `found` stays false until the negate flag from step 9 flips it to true.

Root cause. The code treats the negated-class success from step 10 as if one real string byte had been consumed. It therefore advances `s` even though `s` still points at the filename's NUL terminator, leaving `s` one byte past the heap buffer and moving `p` to the remaining pattern tail `*-]`.

Sink. The same recursive frame now reenters the `*` case on the tail `*-]`. Reading `*s` here dereferences the byte immediately after the 176-byte region `[0x60f000000130, 0x60f0000001e0)` allocated at `Curl_ftp_parselist:358`, exactly matching the saved ASan report.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: allocation_context is the LIST-entry buffer in `Curl_ftp_parselist`, while the missing guard is the later `s++` in `loop()` that steps past that buffer.

poc.trigger: The staged 817-byte `poc` (SHA-256 `a5f78852ee518f32703762620d5f59c5894f35986dc062d05394f7d5328c07fe`) is a curl_fuzzer TLV stream whose type-1 URL ends with `/[-list/*[!*-]*-]`, whose type-31 second-socket payload begins with `total 20` and drives `Curl_ftp_parselist()` through the UNIX filename parser on at least one entry, and whose type-33 raw value is non-zero. In the saved vulnerable run, curl enters wildcard mode, routes that LIST body into `Curl_ftp_parselist()`, records `parser->offsets.filename`, and `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` invokes `Curl_fnmatch()` on the resulting filename. The leading `*` eventually retries `[!*-]*-]` on the filename terminator, `loop()` advances `s` past the heap buffer, and the next `*s` read crashes at `lib/curl_fnmatch.c:326`.

format.name: curl_fuzzer TLV stream
format.contract: The witness must be a curl_fuzzer TLV stream with a type-1 URL whose final path component is `*[!*-]*-]`, a type-31 second-socket FTP LIST payload whose first byte is non-digit so `Curl_ftp_parselist()` stays on the UNIX parser and reaches `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` on at least one parsed filename, and a type-33 `WILDCARDMATCH` TLV with any non-zero 32-bit value so curl enters wildcard mode.
